note: Schematic approximations. Authored from a written specification, not derived from BodyParts3D, Z-Anatomy, or any imaging or cadaveric data. Indicative paths only.

deviations.why: Radius.l stops at Z=0.856, proximal to the carpal tunnel at Z~0.85, and its Y range bottoms out at -0.027, so the tunnel was not reachable without an offset that no longer tracked the geometry. The retinaculum is the roof of the tunnel and localises it exactly.
The palm is outside Radius.l's bounding box. Anchored to the radius, the terminus landed dorsal to the metacarpals rather than in the palm.

deviations.what: distal forearm, palmar to the radius
deviations.why: Without it the curve grazed the palmar surface of the distal radius.
Guyon's canal is bounded by the pisiform. Ulna.l's bounding box is skewed by the olecranon and does not localise the canal.
As for the median terminus: the hand is outside Ulna.l's bounding box.
The nerve turned lateral too early and was anterior to the humerus over part of the spiral groove, which is the opposite of the relationship that matters here.

This is the tightest path in the set. At a 6 mm radius the tube is 12 mm across and the costoclavicular space in this model is narrower than that on the direct line: the retroclavicular route pinches to 4.4 mm and the lateral route to 0.8 mm against the clavicle. The corridor that does fit runs above the second rib and then behind the clavicle, and holding the curve inside it needs three clavicle control points rather than one.

deviations.what: axilla lowered from Z~1.38 to Z~1.31
deviations.why: The axilla point sat above the pectoralis minor point, so the path folded back on itself and the bezier overshot into the rib cage.

deviations.what: exits the greater sciatic notch posteriorly
deviations.why: The anterior route is solid bone: measured clearance to the ischium there is 0.1-3 mm against a 5 mm tube. The nerve now passes posterior to the ilium into the gluteal region, which is also where it actually runs.

deviations.what: ankle, deep to the extensor retinaculum
deviations.why: Without it the curve overshot anteriorly out of the shin between the leg and the foot, and the terminus dived into the tarsus.

deviations.what: medial knee, anterior to the condyles
deviations.why: The curve from mid-thigh to the medial leg bowed through the femoral condyles and the tibia.
